hypothesis: Multiple v_calendar_1 train failures share a single mechanism: the agent misreads event-time fields returned by the gym (list_events / get_event / query_freebusy) when seeded events carry a `+00:00` (or `Z`) offset suffix in `dateTime` while their `timeZone` field is a non-UTC IANA name like `America/New_York`. The gym's seed SQL preserves the offset string verbatim (e.g. `('event-corrected-001', ..., '2025-10-06T09:00:00+00:00', ..., 'America/New_York', 'America/New_York', ...)`) but the DB's `start_timezone` column is the wall-clock authority. The current section 2 of GOOGLE_CALENDAR_API_NOTES covers the WRITING direction only, so the agent applies the same ISO-8601 instinct when READING and treats `14:00:00+00:00` as 14:00 UTC = 9 AM ET, then concludes there is no conflict with a 2-4:30 PM ET meeting. This drove (a) task_20251203_091910 (missed the focus-time + sick-leave conflicts; the verifier expected the Oct 20 Focus Time rescheduled to 16:30-17:30 ET and the Nov 22 Sprint #3 moved to Nov 23 — pass rate 4/6 = 0.67), (b) task_20251202_190412 (verifier_conflicting_events_removed failed: 1 conflicting event left because the agent didn't see it as a conflict — pass rate 4/5 = 0.8), and (c) task_20260106_143218 (Shadow Sync start-time computation needed reading the Sprint Planning event's end time in ET — pass rate 3/7 = 0.43). A capability-path edit that extends section 2 with a READING-direction rule (interpret `dateTime`'s local-naive part as wall-clock in `timeZone`, ignoring any offset suffix) should let the agent correctly detect conflicts and compute relative times in one coherent change.

hypothesis: Multiple v_calendar_2 train failures share a single mechanism: when `create_event` succeeds (gym returns 200 OK with an event JSON containing `id` plus `status: "confirmed"`), optional fields like `attachments` may come back as `[]` (the gym requires `supportsAttachments: true` to persist them) and `conferenceData` may come back as `null` (the gym does not echo the `createRequest` block back). The agent misreads these empty echoes as 'the create failed', and calls `create_event` a SECOND time with a 'corrected' payload. The DB now contains two rows that both match the verifier's WHERE clause, so the COUNT(*)=1 checks return actual=2 and fail. This drove (a) task_20260106_152415 (`event verifier` actual=2 vs 1; agent called `create_event` 5 times trying to attach attachments / fix conferenceData) and (b) task_20251203_194320 (`strategy_kickoff_created` actual=2 vs 1; first create returned a full event JSON with id but attachments came back empty, agent retried with a near-identical payload). A capability-path edit extending section 5 of GOOGLE_CALENDAR_API_NOTES with explicit guidance on (i) the success signal (`id` + `status: confirmed`), (ii) why `attachments: []` / `conferenceData: null` echoes do NOT imply persistence failure, and (iii) using `patch_event` against the returned `id` to add or correct fields, should fix this in one coherent change.

trust.evidence_anchor: Google Calendar API + HTTP/REST documented semantics: POST /calendars/{calendarId}/events (create_event) is NOT idempotent; success is signalled by an HTTP 200 OK with the Event resource JSON whose `id` is the server-assigned event identifier and whose `status` is one of {`confirmed`, `tentative`, `cancelled`}. Documented Event-resource field behaviors: `attachments` are only persisted when the request carries `supportsAttachments=true` (otherwise the server discards them, leaving the response's `attachments` array empty); `conferenceData.createRequest` is a one-shot request token that is consumed at create time and does not echo back into the response unless the conference solution itself is already provisioned. These are external API contracts (RFC 9110 §9.2.2 for POST non-idempotence; Google Calendar API v3 reference for the `supportsAttachments` flag and createRequest semantics), not patterns extracted from the failing rows.

hypothesis: Multiple v_calendar_3 train failures share a single mechanism: when the agent builds the `attendees: [...]` list for `create_event`, it (a) shortens the canonical canonical email to a bare first-name local-part (e.g. `adam@techcorp.com` instead of `adam.anderson@techcorp.com`) and (b) passes just the first name as `displayName` (e.g. `'Carol'` instead of `'Carol White'`). The gym's `attendees.user_id` column is populated by joining `attendees.email` to `users.email`, and verifiers check both `attendees.user_id IN (...)` and `attendees.displayname = '<full name>'` against the seeded `users.name`. Bare local-parts return no row from the join, leaving `attendees.user_id` NULL; short displayNames mis-match the verifier's exact-equality string. This drove (a) task_20251203_194320 (iter3 vpr 0.75, `check_attendees` expected 3 / actual 0 because agent used `adam@`, `brent@`, `bob@`) and (b) task_20260107_093643 (iter3 vpr 0.75, `check_attendee` expected `Carol White`/`accepted`, actual 0 because agent used `displayName: 'Carol'`). A capability-path edit that extends section 5 of GOOGLE_CALENDAR_API_NOTES with an explicit ATTENDEE-FIELD-COMPLETION block (canonical full email, full-name displayName, lookup via `get_user_by_email` / `list_users` when the prompt names a person only by first name) should fix these in one coherent change.

Verifier SQL on that task asserts `calendars.default_reminders LIKE '%\"method\":\"email\"%' AND default_reminders LIKE '%\"minutes\":60%'`, so `calendars.default_reminders` IS the gym's persistence target for calendar-level default reminders. The matcher fires only on structural prompt-text/tool-spec features (oracle tool list, prompt regex, assistant-text regex) — not on patterns induced from N failing rows.
trust.rollback_when: Frontier calendar train accuracy drops below v_calendar_3 (22/30 = 0.7333). Watch for: (i) a previously passing task whose tool set is update_calendar-only AND whose prompt mentions a default reminder AND whose assistant response coincidentally contains inability markers regresses because the injected hint nudges an `update_calendar(defaultReminders=...)` call that the gym then 4xx-rejects, eating extra turns. Among the five v0 train tasks whose tools_used contained update_calendar (task_20260121_171247, task_20260105_124102, task_20260107_193032, task_20260106_170952, task_20260105_140440), only task_20260121_171247's user prompt mentions reminders, so the matcher does not fire on the other four. (ii) The guard fires legitimately but the gym does NOT accept defaultReminders on `update_calendar` — in which case task_20260121_171247 stays at vpr 0.5 (no regression, no improvement) and the rollback bar is not tripped.

trust.fallback: On any matcher-false the handler is never reached and behaviour is byte-identical to v_calendar_3. Decision.inject_context is appended to ctx.shared['post_llm_inject'] and surfaced as a SystemMessage on the NEXT turn — no tool call is blocked, no tool arg rewritten, no orchestrator behaviour changed. If the agent ignores the nudge, the task stays at v_calendar_3's vpr 0.5 with one extra SystemMessage of ~110 tokens consumed.
